title: Of the Inevitable Fruit of Good and Evil Actions
summary: On the fifth day, the Fifth Wazir argued on the balance of justice before King Azadbakht. Bakhtiyar stepped forward and delivered his discourse:
keywords: of the issues of good and evil actions
full_text:
On the fifth day, the Fifth Wazir argued on the balance of justice before King Azadbakht. Bakhtiyar stepped forward and delivered his discourse:

'Sire, the universe is governed by an unbending law of moral balance that no emperor can decree away. As a man sows, so shall he reap: he who plants sweet pomegranate seeds will gather sweet fruit, and he who scatters thorns will harvest only briars that tear his own flesh.

An evil deed may seem to triumph for an hour, cloaked in gold and protected by armies; but its root is rotten, and it carries the seed of its own downfall within its chest. Injustice creates an army of invisible adversaries in the hearts of the oppressed.

A good deed, by contrast, even if performed in secret by a humble water-carrier, radiates like a candle in the dark. It wins the allegiance of souls, disarms malice, and calls down the blessings of the heavens.

The tyrant imagines that his sword makes him safe, but history records that the throne built on cruelty collapses into dust, while the king who rules with justice and mercy lives forever in the grateful memory of his people, as shown in the chronicle of King Dadbin.'
moral: Every deed bears fruit according to its seed; benevolence returns as a blessing, and malice as ruin.
